title: Busko's work rules out plate defects in the transients

plain: In the 1950s, astronomers photographed the night sky on glass plates, and a researcher named Beatriz Villarroel has studied brief points of light on those plates that appear and then vanish. Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that work by another scientist, Ivo Busko, shows these patterns are not chemical stains or flaws in the plates. As Michels tells it, the light really did pass through the telescope's optics, which would mean something real was briefly up there.
